turns.t: Good morning. Before we start, can I just check your name? Is it Mr Desmond Achterberg?
That's me. Desmond is fine, though. Nobody calls me Mr Achterberg except the bank.
Desmond it is. Your GP asked me to take a look. What's your own understanding of why you're here?
Honestly? It's my left foot, and it's probably nothing. My daughter nagged me into coming.
Daughters usually have good instincts. Has anything stopped you doing what you normally do?
Not really. I still walk the dog every morning. I just wanted her to stop going on about it.
Good for you. Now, a few questions about the nerves. Do you have any weakness in the leg?
No weakness. It has never given way on me or anything.
How about your balance? Have you had any falls lately?
No, I haven't fallen. I'm steady enough, thanks.
Last of the nerve questions. Any trouble with your bladder or bowels?
No, nothing like that.
Good, those are the ones I worry about most. Do you have any other health conditions?
Type 2 diabetes. Diet only so far, the GP keeps an eye on it.
And does anybody else in the family have diabetes?
My father did. He had diabetes for years before he passed.
Thanks for telling me. Do you smoke?
About ten cigarettes a day. I know, I know.
I'm not going to nag, your daughter has that covered. What about alcohol?
A couple of pints on a Saturday at the club. That's my lot.
Fair. And are you taking any tablets at the moment?
Not a thing. I keep away from them where I can.
Any allergies to medicines or anything else?
None that I know of.
Good. I'm going to check your blood pressure and pulse, then test the feeling in your feet.
Fine. Is this going to hurt?
Not at all. Blood pressure is 136 over 84, and your pulse is 72.
Is that good?
Pretty reasonable. Now close your eyes and say yes each time you feel this wisp of cotton wool touch your foot.
Yes. Yes. Hang on. Was that the toes? I couldn't tell.
Thank you. The feeling is reduced in the toes of your left foot, compared with the right.
Ah. Well. Is it serious?
Let me explain it plainly. Nerves are like electrical cables, and years of high sugar can wear away the insulation, so the signal gets fuzzy. It looks like early nerve damage from the diabetes.
Can it be fixed?
It can be slowed down a lot. Step one is bloods. I'd like to order blood tests, for your sugar control and your vitamin B12, since a low B12 can do something similar.
Today?
The nurse can take them on your way out. Then I'd like to see you in two weeks, to go through the results together.
Two weeks. Right. I'll bring my daughter, she'll want to hear it for herself.
Please do. And look after those feet in the meantime. Check them every evening, and wear slippers indoors.
Understood. Thank you, doctor.
Take care, Desmond. Give the dog my regards.
